text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening stance: \"No, driverless cars should not be developed\"","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a definite position right away, so the reader immediately knows what the essay is arguing."},{"evidence":"three separate body paragraphs on danger, lawsuits, and laziness","quality":"argument organization","description":"It develops the position in distinct points rather than drifting among unrelated comments."},{"evidence":"\"Having driverless cars can be dangerous\" followed by examples from the article","quality":"use of evidence","description":"It pulls in article details to support claims instead of relying only on general opinion."},{"evidence":"\"the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault—the driver or the manufactuer?\"","quality":"counterargument awareness","description":"It acknowledges a realistic legal concern raised by the article and uses it to strengthen the argument."},{"evidence":"concluding paragraph restating the negative position","quality":"conclusion","description":"It ends by summarizing the argument and reinforcing the writer's stance."},{"evidence":"frequent sentence-to-sentence linking like \"Not only...\" and \"Although...\"","quality":"coherence","description":"It connects ideas enough to keep the essay readable and guide the reader through the argument."}]}
